study_info.title: Calcitriol in the Treatment of Postmenopausal Osteoporosis
study_info.authors: JOHN F. ALOIA, M.D. ASHOK VASWANI, M.D. JAMES K. YEH, Ph.D. KENNETH ELLIS, Ph.D. SEIICHI YASUMURA, Ph.D. STANTON H. COHN, Ph.D.
study_info.study_design: 24-month double-blind, randomized, parallel clinical trial. The method of randomization is not specified.
study_info.inclusion_criteria: Women with postmenopausal osteoporosis between the ages of 50 and 80 years, diagnosed by the presence of at least one non-traumatic vertebral compression fracture, otherwise healthy.
study_info.exclusion_criteria: Hepatic or renal disease, malignancy, malabsorption syndrome, parathyroid or thyroid disorders, inflammatory arthritis, alcoholism, overt vitamin D deficiency, a history of renal lithiasis, allergy to tetracycline, insulin-dependent diabetes, previous long-term hospitalization, any other disorder known to affect bone metabolism, intake of certain drugs including glucocorticoids, anticonvulsants, estrogens, sodium fluoride, calcium supplements, and pharmacologic doses of vitamin D.
study_info.study_setting: Winthrop-University Hospital, Mineola, New York, and Brookhaven National Laboratory, Upton, New York.
study_info.source_of_recruitment: Media releases and letters to physicians.
study_info.dropout_reasons: Placebo group: myocardial infarction (1), dizziness and nausea believed due to the drug (1). Calcitriol group: myocardial infarction (1), psychiatric disturbance (1), death of a spouse (1), change in residence (1), discouragement when a new fracture occurred (1).

minimal_units.intervention_details: Each patient received 400 IU of vitamin D daily. Dietary calcium intake was assessed by a three-day diet history and patients were instructed in a 1,000-mg calcium intake. All patients received two capsules per day, one before breakfast and the second before dinner. The capsules contained either 0.25 μg of calcitriol or a matching placebo. The following stepwise escalation in dose was permitted: after two weeks to two capsules twice daily, at one month to three capsules twice daily, and after six weeks to the maximum of four capsules twice daily. The investigator also had the option of stepwise escalation of one capsule instead of two every two weeks. The dosage schedule was to be modified to control hypercalciuria (greater than 400 mg of calcium per 24-hour urine sample), if lowering dietary calcium intake was ineffective. If significant hypercalcemia developed (greater than 11.6 mg/dl), the drug was to be temporarily discontinued and the dose was initiated later at one capsule daily.
minimal_units.intervention_frequency: Initial: two capsules per day, titrated up to four capsules twice daily as tolerated
minimal_units.adherence_to_intervention: The mean number of capsules for the placebo group was 7.6, indicating adherence of the investigators to the protocol in dosage titration.

outcomes.domain_match: Matches 'all-cause mortality' domain (death of a spouse is not patient death, but no patient death is explicitly reported).
